html:
SMTO-BOOT-0038 — A model's answer had no structured data for the benchmark to check

GUID: 9325f33c-9078-4d5f-b616-330141818f36
Slug: boot-benchmark-json-missing
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • One benchmark question asked the model to reply in a strict data format, but its answer contained none. That question is marked as failed; the rest of the benchmark carries on.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In src/vllm/results/ (or the folder you chose with --results-dir), open the newest file whose name starts with benchmark- and doesn't end in .md. Find the failed question's “text” entry. That entry holds the model's exact answer, so you can see what it wrote instead.
  2. If the answer stops mid-sentence, count it as a real fail for that model. Each question limits how long the reply can be, and an unfinished reply can't contain the complete data.
  3. If the answer begins with the model thinking out loud, make sure your command doesn't include --no-no-think, then run the benchmark again. By default the benchmark tells models not to show their thinking, which keeps their answers in the requested format.

What success looks like

  • In the .md report, that question shows PASS, or its failure no longer says “could not parse”.

If it still fails

  • If the model keeps answering in plain text, that is its genuine result. Share the report files with the person who maintains your model setup, and don't change the benchmark questions to make a model pass.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • extract_json_object found no parseable JSON and no {...} span in a model response for a benchmark case with numeric checks, so that case was recorded as failed (“numeric check could not parse JSON: no JSON object found”).

What this means

  • JSON extraction cannot parse the whole benchmark response and finds no braced object to attempt as a fallback. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • JSON extraction cannot parse the whole benchmark response and finds no braced object to attempt as a fallback.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the saved response and expected benchmark contract; this error does not establish model-server unavailability.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the failing case's "text" field in the run's benchmark-*.json under the results directory. Typical causes are prose instead of JSON, output cut off at the case's max_tokens from benchmark_prompts.json (no closing brace), or reasoning text when run with --no-no-think. Treat it as a model-output failure; do not relax the check or edit the prompt to make a model pass.
  • Inspect the response and expected benchmark result contract.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid benchmark response is extracted without invented missing fields.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
